analysis.title: The RIC Report: The rotation is accelerating
key_insights: Since the June 2026 AI peak, rotation into unloved assets and factors (value, SMID, real assets, yield) has accelerated. A 50/50 mix of semiconductors and neocloud stocks is flat YTD.
AI leaders have lost value since the June peak at an annualized pace equal to their rate of gain since Q4 2022. The S&P 500 rallied 21% annualized in 2022-2026 and has been flat since the June peak.

Value rallied at a 14% annualized rate in 2022-2026 and 20% since the June peak. Equal-weight S&P 500 returned 12% CAGR then 15%. Dynamic commodities returned 21% then 13%. Loans/CLOs returned 7-8% then 5%.

US growth stocks lagged value by 28ppt in 2026 so far and by 18ppt over three years (87% vs 69%). Value ETFs are on pace for a second straight year of record inflows ($91bn vs $67bn for growth). Equal-weight funds added $16bn YTD while megacap growth funds shed $1.1bn.

Average trailing quarterly S&P 500 ex-Mag 7 EPS ($2.99) now exceeds Mag 7 ($2.52), the widest gap in favor of the 493 since 2023. Hartnett notes AI equity concentration has likely peaked near 40%, the level seen in prior bubbles.
Russell 1000 Value beat Russell 1000 Growth by 10.4ppt in October, the highest on record.

Midterm read: since 1950 the S&P 500 has risen in each of the twelve months after midterms, averaging +15%. BofA expects gridlock even with a Democratic wave, which it sees as positive for stocks, and little change in tariff policy.

US economy remains strong: September payrolls were 165k vs 70k estimate, four-week average jobless claims are below 195k (lowest since 1969), ISM Manufacturing is 56, the BofA Global Earnings Revisions Ratio is above 1.0 (US 1.01), and over 75% of S&P 500 companies beat EPS estimates for a third straight quarter.

Positioning is outweighing fundamentals. MSFT beat adjusted EPS by 4% with 23% YoY growth and fell 0.2%. WELL grew FFO/share 25% and fell 6%. KO beat by 3% and fell over 1.5%. GLW grew adjusted EPS 36%, beat, and fell over 1%. The BofA Bull & Bear Indicator is 7.2, closer to a sell signal.

BofA suggests a tactical focus on income: Treasuries (4.8% average ETF yield), AAA CLOs (4.8%), MLPs (4.3%), options income ETFs (7.9% average yield in the list header, over 10% in the text), and EM debt (7.0%) as a play on potential oil peace.

A new Fed hiking cycle is underway. BofA Economics expects one more hike this year and one more next year. Scenarios exist where long-term rates reach the 6-7% warning level, which BofA calls unlikely. Chris Flanagan favors tactical Treasury trades, Hartnett says own until 4.5%, and Ciana warns bond bulls of big support at 4.8%.
AAA CLOs offered a 28% 5-year total return with a 3% max drawdown. BofA initiated ratings on 17 options income ETFs.

Technical view: the US 2Y yield tested and held uptrend support, then rebounded after hot CPI. A close above 4.83% targets 4.95%, 5.07% and possibly above 5.26%. This week's low near 4.50% is the ideal support.
The Dynamic Prudent Yield strategy is invested only in CLOs/leveraged loans (17%) and cash (83%) in November. It is +0.9% YTD vs US Aggregate -0.6% and TLT -2.8%.

Equity ETF valuation: median ETF forward P/E is 15.3x, 0.1sd above average and the lowest since April 2025. Health care is the most expensive sector at +1.5sd. EM ex-China fell to -1.4sd. Value is the most expensive factor at +1.4sd and buybacks the cheapest at -0.6sd.

BofA Global Economics sees the midterms reshaping the policy outlook, with more AI regulation likely after voters passed 40 of 41 ballot measures opposing data centers. Base case is two more Fed hikes, in December and March.

Savita Subramanian's team finds Q3 beats are broad but not rewarded. Q3 EPS growth is tracking 30% YoY (another exhibit shows median EPS growth tracking 14%). Beat-on-EPS-and-sales names outperformed by only 90bp the next day vs a 1.4% historical average. A 20% cut to 2027 AI capex alone could reduce 2027 S&P 500 EPS by 7-8%.

High Yield & Loan Strategy sees credit-funded AI capex peaking at about $685 billion in 2027 (+31%), mostly from private credit. HY gross issuance is expected to rise 3% to $340 billion and leveraged loan issuance to rise 18% to $470 billion.

NVDA: Vivek Arya's team keeps Buy and $350 PO after the company's independent review of reported foreign-intelligence concerns. The team calls it a new overhang, not yet an earnings event. After a 37% correction the semiconductor index trades at 13.7x forward earnings, a 22% discount to the S&P 500.

Andrew Obin's team argues local opposition to data centers will move construction rather than stop it, by analogy to fracking. About 60% of the US data center pipeline would be unaffected even if all new governors pause construction.
Consumer: savings rate is down to 3.8%. BofA is Neutral on TPR and reiterates Buy on MNST ($54 PO, sales +16.6% YoY), PRMB ($29) and CELH ($37). TAP stays Underperform at $36 after a miss.

MP Materials: Buy and $85 PO maintained. Q3 adjusted EBITDA of $41.1 million beat the team's $24.5 million estimate, though a one-time $31.6 million stockpiled concentrate sale drove most of the beat. Net cash is $402 million.
Nuclear: DOE targets 10 new large reactors with more than $200 billion of financing authority, loans covering up to 80% of eligible costs and 30-50% investment tax credits.

Defensive income roundtable: PGR (Buy, 6.1% yield; Shanker forecasts an annual special dividend of $13.50/share, about $8bn total), VZ (Neutral, 6.2% yield; Funk expects $22.6bn 2027 FCF vs about $11.5bn dividends) and DOC (Buy, 6.0% yield; 77% cash payout ratio).

BofA house view: Investment Strategy stays risk-off until global rate hikes end, 10-year UST yield falls below 4.5% and oil falls below $80/bbl. Year-end S&P 500 target is 7,400 and 12-month target is 7,700. BofA prefers large cap value, cyclicals and capex takers.

BofA keeps its Brent forecast at $96/bbl for 2H26 and $91/bbl for full-year 2026, easing to $80 in 2027. A ceasefire could push Brent toward $80 or lower, a 'neither war nor peace' status quo could keep prices near triple digits, and renewed US-Iran conflict could push Brent toward $150 in 2027.

October 2026 review: global equities -1.6%, MSCI EM -8.0%, Nasdaq -5.3%, communication services -15.1%, IT -6.8%. Energy (+14.0%), staples and utilities led. WTI rose 15.2%, Brent 13.6%, gold fell 6.2%, and 30-year Treasuries gained 5.5%.

earnings_insights: Q3 2026 S&P 500 reporting: nearly 90% of companies reported and over 75% beat EPS estimates (reported results), the third straight quarter, last seen in 2021. EPS growth is tracking 30% YoY per Savita Subramanian's team, while Exhibit 12 shows median EPS growth tracking 14% YoY as of 11/6/2026.
MSFT adjusted EPS grew 23% YoY, a 4% beat (reported), and the stock fell 0.2% the next day.
WELL reported FFO/share growth of 25% YoY (reported) and the stock fell 6% the next day.
KO beat adjusted EPS by 3% with 11% YoY growth (reported), and the stock fell over 1.5%.
GLW reported 36% YoY adjusted EPS growth, beat estimates (reported), and fell over 1% by the close.
MP Materials Q3 adjusted EBITDA reported at $41.1 million vs BofA estimate of $24.5 million. A one-time $31.6 million sale of stockpiled concentrate drove most of the beat.
MNST Q3 sales grew 16.6% YoY (reported). TAP missed Q3 earnings (reported).
BofA Dynamic Prudent Yield strategy: not applicable. For Verizon, BofA estimates (forecast) 2027 free cash flow of about $22.6 billion vs about $11.5 billion of dividend payments.
Beats on both EPS and sales outperformed by only 90bp the next day, below the 1.4% historical average (reported).
